policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV's 'tossed to and fro' does not distinguish the qere and ketiv forms, and no mapped textual note selects either reading; retain the documented qere base fallback.
ASV's 'her sun is gone down' does not distinguish the qere and ketiv forms, and no mapped textual note selects either reading; retain the documented qere base fallback.
ASV's main text reads 'I will strengthen thee for good,' while the mapped textual-variant note assigns 'release' to another reading; the main wording therefore selects the qere base reading.
ASV twice renders the lemma as plural ('Thy words'), distinguishing and selecting the plural ketiv reading דבריך over the singular qere base.
